title: Chapter 11 — The Mark That Wasn’t Ours

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Chapter title. Leave a clean beat before story begins.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They found the first forged notch on the eighth day.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: It was in a narrow cut between two dye-houses that had opened overnight and already started to close at the edges. Two clean marks sat at the base of the left wall, cut at the same depth and angle Ninsun used. Beside them someone had added a third—slightly deeper, the edges still sharp with stone dust.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg saw it first. He stopped so suddenly that En-HEH-doo nearly walked into his back.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun crouched and studied the three marks without touching them. After a long moment she shook her head.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: The third isn't mine. The angle's wrong. Whoever cut it was stronger in the wrist and less patient.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: So either we're not the only ones marking, or the fucking city learned the system.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek ran his thumb along the third notch. The stone dust came away clean. Fresh. Maybe an hour old. Maybe less. He looked up the short passage. It ended in the usual blank wall that would probably be ordinary brick again by evening.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: We mark our own and we move. If we start chasing every cut that isn't ours, we'll still be here when the streets forget our names.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun carefully added the location to her ugly, incomplete map, noting the forged third mark with a small cross. Her handwriting had gotten smaller and tighter over the last few days, as if she were trying to fit more city onto less paper.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They backed out. Behind them the passage had already narrowed enough that a man would have to turn sideways to enter. By the time they reached the main street it looked like a shallow service recess any local would have sworn had always been there.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A boy from the lower market found them at the cheap room they were using. He couldn't have been more than fourteen, all elbows and caution. He held out a folded scrap of parchment like it might bite.

lines.speaker: Messenger Boy
lines.text: Man said to give this to the ones cutting marks on the walls,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg crouched until he was eye level with the boy.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The boy frowned as though the question itself was unreasonable.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg reached into his pouch and produced a small bronze coin.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The boy looked at the coin.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The boy scratched behind one ear.

lines.speaker: Messenger Boy
lines.text: Everyone around here has dirty hands.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He held up his own fingers.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The nails were packed with dust.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun looked up from the table.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The boy looked genuinely frustrated now.

lines.speaker: Messenger Boy
lines.text: He stood where the alley bends.

lines.speaker: Messenger Boy
lines.text: Like he already knew I'd come.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg exchanged a glance with Zeek.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The boy finally accepted the coin.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The boy frowned, trying to remember.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He hurried down the stairs before anyone could stop him.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg remained at the doorway until the footsteps disappeared.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Then he quietly slid the bolt across the door.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He didn't wait for payment. He was already gone when BAH-lahg stepped into the lane to look for him.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: One line, written in a neat, anonymous hand:

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: STOP MARKING WHAT DOES NOT BELONG TO YOU.
lines.note: Written text (ledger/inscription/journal, not in Bel-iddin's hand). Cold, deliberate read.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: No signature. No threat beyond the words themselves. The parchment was the same cheap stock the lower scribes used for temporary notes.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He held it toward the lamp.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: Whoever wrote this expected we'd read it.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: People usually expect that from letters.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun stood and crossed the room.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She took the parchment without asking.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: For nearly a minute she said nothing.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Then she reached into her satchel and removed the map.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She laid the warning beside it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek watched her eyes move between the two.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: I feel like scholars are inventing reasons to be frightened.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: I leave exactly this much room at the top of every page.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek picked up the note again.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: You think someone copied your habits.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: …someone has seen enough of my work to imitate it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: That silence worried Zeek more than anything she could have said.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-HEH-doo read it over his shoulder.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: Or the city hired better messengers,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun took the scrap and set it beside her map without comment. After a moment she drew a small, precise box around the entire western dye-house district and wrote a single word inside it:

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Written text (ledger/inscription/journal, not in Bel-iddin's hand). Cold, deliberate read.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek watched her work. The journal was still in his pack. Four days had become five. He had not opened it. The decision still felt like the only part of this place he actually controlled.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He flexed his left hand inside the linen. The mark was quiet.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Outside, somewhere in the lower districts, another passage was probably opening. Or closing. Or deciding which marks it would allow to remain.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They had drawn a line on the city.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Whether that someone lived above the streets or beneath them, none of the four could yet say.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: But for the first time since opening the tomb, they no longer felt like explorers.
